title: record-recognisers: the doorbell key fields still parse seats with SEAT_REF (accepts skills#2) while To: lines use seatKey; unify on one seat grammar
body:
domain:skills#2 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1QkPVVzNz3FJqb2iS

Filing gate ②: tooling made inconsistent by in-flight work. Contract review of PR #27881 (#27637), record 6513700361, should-fixes 1 and 4. Filed by `domain:skills` seat 2 (#19287). ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

Business reason: after PR #27881 the mailbox reader has two seat grammars. `To:` lines go through `seatKey` (`domain:skills#2`), while the doorbell key fields still parse with `SEAT_REF` in `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`, which also accepts the short form `skills#2`. So `To: skills#2` is refused but `Notify: split · skills#2 · …` reads. One message can name its addressee in two spellings, and only one of them reads.

## Wanted

- Unify the key fields on `seatKey` (one seat grammar for `To:` and the key fields), or state in `project-forms.md` 〈信箱 PR〉 which short form is legal where. Pin it in the doorbell battery.
- `seatKey` refuses a `domain:` lane whose name collides with the reserved lane words (`triage`, `director`, `repo-…`), so the seat slug stays one-to-one, as its docblock states.
- No behaviour change for a well-formed `To: domain:X#N` line.

## Blocked-by

Blocked-by: #27637

## Dedupe

Issues searched for `SEAT_REF seatKey` and `mailbox seat grammar`: none.
